problem: TIER1/SECURITY — Per-account rate limiting is dead code: app.UseRateLimiter() is registered BEFORE app.UseAuthentication(), so httpContext.User carries no claims when the 'runs' and 'saves' partition callbacks run. Every authenticated user collapses into the per-IP fallback partition, and users behind a shared NAT throttle each other while a single attacker with rotating IPs bypasses per-account limits entirely.
action: Reorder the middleware pipeline so authentication executes before the rate limiter, guaranteeing ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier is populated when partition keys are computed.
location: services/backend/src/Aumbrye.Api/Program.cs (Lines 209-213 / middleware pipeline; Lines 141-165 / 'runs' and 'saves' rate-limit policies)
implementation: In Program.cs change the order to: app.UseMiddleware<VersionHeaderMiddleware>(); app.UseCors("web"); app.UseAuthentication(); app.UseAuthorization(); app.UseRateLimiter(); Endpoint-scoped RequireRateLimiting policies execute inside the rate-limiter middleware, so once it sits after UseAuthentication the FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier) lookup in both policies resolves. Add an integration test that issues 11 CreateRun calls with two different bearer tokens from the same IP and asserts the second account is NOT throttled by the first account's partition.

problem: TIER1/SECURITY — UseForwardedHeaders is enabled with no KnownProxies/KnownNetworks restriction, so any client can spoof X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto. Because the 'public', 'runs' and 'saves' rate-limit partitions fall back to Connection.RemoteIpAddress (which forwarded-headers middleware rewrites), an attacker can rotate a fake XFF header to mint unlimited rate-limit partitions and bypass throttling on auth endpoints.
action: Restrict forwarded-header processing to the actual reverse proxy, or gate it behind configuration that is only set in the deployed environment.
implementation: var fwd = new ForwardedHeadersOptions { ForwardedHeaders = ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedFor | ForwardedHeaders.XForwardedProto, ForwardedForHeaderName = "X-Forwarded-For" }; fwd.KnownProxies.Clear(); fwd.KnownNetworks.Clear(); foreach (var proxy in builder.Configuration.GetSection("ForwardedHeaders:KnownProxies").Get<string[]>() ?? []) fwd.KnownProxies.Add(IPAddress.Parse(proxy)); app.UseForwardedHeaders(fwd); When no proxy is configured (local dev), skip UseForwardedHeaders entirely so RemoteIpAddress is always the socket peer.

problem: TIER1/CRITICAL BUG — RedisLeaderboardStore.TrimAsync deletes the BEST runs instead of the worst. The sorted set is scored ascending by elapsedSeconds (rank 0 = fastest run). Trim removes ranks 0..(count-Max-1), i.e. the fastest entries, so once a board exceeds 1000 entries the top of the leaderboard is permanently destroyed on every subsequent submit.
action: Trim from the tail of the sorted set (slowest times), never the head.
implementation: Replace the body with: private static Task TrimAsync(IDatabase db, RedisKey key) => db.SortedSetRemoveRangeByRankAsync(key, MaxEntriesPerKey, -1); This keeps ranks 0..999 (the 1000 fastest) and removes everything slower in one round trip (the pre-count SortedSetLengthAsync call becomes unnecessary — Redis no-ops when the range is empty). Add a unit/integration test: insert 1001 entries with increasing scores, submit once more, assert the entry with the lowest score still exists and the highest score was evicted.

problem: TIER1/BUG — Leaderboards accumulate unlimited duplicate entries per player. The Redis member string embeds submittedAt (accountId|unixSeconds|displayName), so every submission of the same run (or of each new run) creates a distinct sorted-set member. One player can occupy all 10 visible rows; SubmitFromRunAsync has no per-run or per-account dedupe and a completed run can be resubmitted forever. InMemoryLeaderboardStore has the same flaw plus a duplicate-rank computation that returns the player's FIRST occurrence, not the submitted entry's rank.
action: Store one best-time entry per account per (biome,tier) key, and make run submission idempotent per runId.
implementation: 1) Change the member format to accountId only (metadata like displayName/submittedAt goes in a companion hash: HSET leaderboard:{biome}:tier{t}:meta {accountId} json). 2) In SubmitScoreAsync use GT semantics: fetch existing score with SortedSetScoreAsync; only ZADD when new elapsed < existing (or use ZADD LT flag available in Redis 6.2: db.SortedSetAddAsync(key, member, score, SortedSetWhen.LessThan)). 3) In SubmitFromRunAsync add a persisted flag on the Run entity (LeaderboardSubmittedAt) and return the previous rank when already submitted. 4) Mirror the same one-entry-per-account rule in InMemoryLeaderboardStore by keying a Dictionary<Guid,LeaderboardEntry> per board key.

problem: TIER1/CRITICAL BUG — Multi-floor loot claims are structurally broken in CompleteRunAsync. Run.LootInstanceIdsJson is populated ONLY at run creation from the floor-1 definition, and the lootMap used for granting is parsed ONLY from the floor the player finished on (input.Floor). Consequences: (a) any legitimate loot claimed on floors 2+ is rejected with 'Unknown loot instance id'; (b) loot claimed on earlier floors but completed on a later floor silently vanishes (persisted-set passes for floor-1 ids, but lootMap lookup misses and GrantLoot 'continue's).
action: Accumulate the union of loot instance ids and item mappings across every floor the run has generated, and validate/grant against that union.
location: services/backend/src/Aumbrye.Application/Services/RunService.cs (Lines 86-98 / CreateRunAsync loot persistence; Lines 173-197 / CompleteRunAsync validation and lootMap; Lines 108-130 / GetDungeonDefinitionAsync)
implementation: 1) Change Run.LootInstanceIdsJson to store a Dictionary<string, {ItemId, Quantity, Floor}> serialized as JSON. 2) In GetDungeonDefinitionAsync, after generating a floor for the first time, merge LootInstanceIds.ParseLoot(json) into that dictionary and SaveChangesAsync (guarded by a per-run lock or optimistic retry). 3) In CompleteRunAsync validate claims against the merged dictionary and build lootMap from it directly instead of re-parsing a single floor's definition JSON — this also removes the expensive regeneration call on the completion hot path. 4) Keep the 64-claim cap but raise it consciously for endless mode or clamp per floor.

problem: TIER1/EXPLOIT — CompleteRunAsync has no concurrency guard: two simultaneous /complete requests for the same run both read Status==Active, both pass validation, and both apply ProgressionApplier (double XP, duplicate loot instances added to the save inventory) before the second SaveChangesAsync wins. There is also no idempotency key, and the Godot client retries POSTs on timeout (api_client.gd MAX_ATTEMPTS=3), making accidental double-completion realistic, not just adversarial.
action: Make run completion atomic and idempotent via optimistic concurrency on the Run row.
implementation: 1) Add a concurrency token: on Run add [Timestamp] byte[] RowVersion (Postgres: modelBuilder.Entity<Run>().Property(r => r.RowVersion).IsRowVersion() using xmin). 2) Perform the status flip FIRST as a guarded update: var updated = await _db.Set<Run>().Where(r => r.Id == runId && r.AccountId == accountId && r.Status == RunStatus.Active).ExecuteUpdateAsync(s => s.SetProperty(r => r.Status, RunStatus.Completed).SetProperty(r => r.CompletedAt, now), ct); if (updated == 0) return 'already completed' (idempotent 200 with previous result is friendlier for the retrying client: cache the CompleteRunResult JSON on the Run row). 3) Only after winning the flip, apply progression and save the blob; wrap in a database transaction so a progression failure rolls the status back.

problem: TIER1/DOS — GetDungeonDefinitionAsync and CompleteRunAsync accept an unbounded floor index. floor=2000000 forces a full procedural generation (up to 48 layout attempts each) per unique value and writes a 24h cache entry per floor, letting one authenticated user burn CPU and flood Redis/memory with garbage keys.
action: Clamp the floor parameter server-side against the run mode's real maximum before generating or caching.
implementation: Define const int MaxFloorsPerRun = 100 (or read from a RunMode config tied to the run row). In both methods: floor = Math.Clamp(floor, 1, MaxFloorsPerRun); return Results.BadRequest for out-of-range instead of silently generating. Additionally cap the number of distinct cached floors per run (track a per-run floor counter on the Run entity) so endless-mode clients cannot pre-generate hundreds of floors in a loop; generation should stay within N floors of the highest completed floor.

problem: TIER1/SECURITY — Steam authentication trusts the client-supplied appId. AuthenticateUserTicket is called with req.AppId straight from the request body, so a ticket minted for ANY app the attacker owns (e.g. a free demo appid) validates successfully and creates/authenticates an Aumbrye account for that Steam user. The Web API key is also sent in a GET query string, which proxies and access logs capture.
action: Pin the appId to server configuration and reject mismatches; move the Steam call to avoid key exposure in URLs.
location: services/backend/src/Aumbrye.Infrastructure/Security/SteamAuthService.cs (Lines 24-31 / ValidateAsync URL construction) and services/backend/src/Aumbrye.Application/Services/AuthService.cs (Lines 126-168 / AuthenticateSteamAsync, Lines 170-198 / LinkSteamAsync)
implementation: 1) Add Steam:AppId to configuration; in AuthService compare: if (appId != _configuredAppId) return new AuthResult(false, Error: "Invalid app.", ErrorStatus: 400); better, drop the appId parameter from the public contract entirely and always use the configured value. 2) In SteamAuthService, keep the partner endpoint but send the key via the 'key' form field of a POST (partner.steam-api.com supports POST for AuthenticateUserTicket) or at minimum scrub the URL from logging/telemetry (OTel http instrumentation records full URLs — add a UrlFilter). 3) Also validate 'ownersteamid' equals 'steamid' if family-sharing should not grant accounts.

problem: TIER1/CRASH — Display-name generation collides with the unique index on Accounts.DisplayName. Register uses 'Wanderer-' + 6 hex chars of the GUID (~16.7M values, birthday collision after ~4800 accounts), and Steam accounts get $"Steam-{steamId}" truncated to 15 chars — SteamID64s are 17 digits, so the truncation keeps only the first 9 digits, which are nearly identical for all accounts (steamids share the 7656119 prefix). The second Steam registration ever created will throw DbUpdateException and surface as an unhandled 500.
action: Generate display names that are unique by construction and handle unique-violation retries.
implementation: 1) Steam: use the LAST digits of the id, e.g. var suffix = (steamId % 1_000_000_000).ToString(); account.DisplayName = $"Steam-{suffix}"; still within 32 chars (the 15-char cap is arbitrary — the column allows 32). 2) Email: keep 'Wanderer-' + 8 chars. 3) Wrap SaveChangesAsync in a retry loop (max 3) that catches DbUpdateException with a unique-violation SqlState (23505) and regenerates the suffix. 4) Add a unit test that forces a collision via a seeded account and asserts registration still succeeds.

problem: TIER1/RUNTIME CRASH RISK — Account.SteamId is declared as C# ulong but mapped to Postgres 'bigint'. Npgsql has no built-in ulong<->bigint mapping; without a ValueConverter, SaveChanges/queries on SteamId throw InvalidCastException at runtime (and even with a raw cast, SteamID64 values above long.MaxValue would overflow — not currently possible for real steamids but unguarded).
action: Add an explicit value converter (ulong <-> long via unchecked bit-cast) for the SteamId column.
implementation: In OnModelCreating: e.Property(x => x.SteamId).HasConversion(new ValueConverter<ulong?, long?>(v => v.HasValue ? unchecked((long)v.Value) : null, v => v.HasValue ? unchecked((ulong)v.Value) : null)).HasColumnType("bigint"); Regenerate the migration snapshot if the store type changes. Add an integration test on the real Npgsql provider (not Sqlite, which masks the issue) that round-trips a SteamId of 76561198000000000 and queries FirstOrDefaultAsync(a => a.SteamId == id).

problem: TIER1/EXPLOIT — The save endpoint trusts the entire client state blob. PUT /saves/current validates only talents; character.level, xp, currencies.gold, inventory contents, itemInstances (including affix rolls and rarity), recipes and flags are accepted verbatim. Any user can craft a max-level save with fabricated legendary items, which then feeds PlayerLevelSnapshot into dungeon generation and indirectly inflates loot budgets. There is also no size cap: a 100 MB JSON body is parsed and stored per account (storage + JSON-parse DoS).
action: Enforce a request size limit and server-side invariants over the save state on every PUT.
implementation: 1) Size: on the endpoint add .WithMetadata(new RequestSizeLimitAttribute(256 * 1024)) or check req.StateJson.Length > 262_144 -> 413. 2) Create a SaveStateValidator that checks: character.level within [1, XpCurve.MaxLevel] AND consistent with character.xp via curve.LevelForXp; gold within [0, 100_000_000]; inventory slot coordinates inside gridWidth/gridHeight with no overlaps; every itemInstances entry re-derivable — recompute AffixRoller.RollWithSeed(instanceId, itemDefId, rollSeed) and reject if rarity/affixes differ from the client's copy (rolls are deterministic, so equipment forgery is fully detectable); recipes/flags ids must exist in catalogs. 3) Return 400 with the first violation; keep TalentValidator as one rule inside the new validator.

problem: TIER1/DATA LOSS — SaveService.ParseState silently replaces a corrupt or non-object save blob with a fresh default character. A truncated row or bad migration wipes a player's progress with no error, no log, and no backup — the next PUT then persists the default over whatever was recoverable.
action: Treat unparseable server-side saves as an error state, not as a fresh character.
implementation: Change ParseState to return a Result: on JsonException log an error with accountId, copy the corrupt JsonData into a new SaveBlobQuarantine table (accountId, capturedAt, rawJson), and have GetCurrentAsync return 500/422 with a distinct error code ('save_corrupt') instead of a default state. Only CompleteRunAsync/CreateRunAsync may fall back to defaults, and only after quarantining. This preserves forensic data and stops silent progression resets.

problem: TIER1/BUG — SteamAuthService is resolved once into a singleton (AddSingleton<ISteamAuthService>(sp => sp.GetRequiredService<SteamAuthService>())) while AddHttpClient<SteamAuthService> registers it transient with a pooled HttpClient whose handler is meant to rotate every 2 minutes. Capturing one instance forever freezes a single HttpMessageHandler: DNS changes to partner.steam-api.com are never observed and the factory's handler-recycling is defeated.
action: Align the lifetime: either make the service consume IHttpClientFactory per call, or register the typed client as the interface implementation without the singleton wrapper.
implementation: Replace with: services.AddHttpClient("steam"); services.AddSingleton<ISteamAuthService, SteamAuthService>(); and change SteamAuthService's constructor to take IHttpClientFactory, calling _httpFactory.CreateClient("steam") inside ValidateAsync. This keeps the cheap singleton (config + logger) while every request gets a factory-managed handler. Alternatively: services.AddHttpClient<ISteamAuthService, SteamAuthService>() and drop both manual registrations (the typed-client registration already maps the interface).

problem: TIER1/PERFORMANCE — RefreshTokenCleanupService materializes every expired token entity into memory (ToListAsync + RemoveRange) each hour. With token rotation on every refresh (a new row per refresh, 30-day expiry + 7-day retention), a modest player base generates hundreds of thousands of rows; loading them for deletion causes GC pressure and long-running transactions.
action: Use set-based deletion instead of entity materialization.
implementation: Replace the body with: var deleted = await db.RefreshTokens.Where(t => t.ExpiresAt < cutoff).ExecuteDeleteAsync(ct); if (deleted > 0) _logger.LogInformation("Deleted {Count} expired refresh tokens.", deleted); (EF Core 7+ ExecuteDeleteAsync issues a single DELETE). Also delete revoked tokens older than the retention window (t.RevokedAt != null && t.RevokedAt < cutoff) — currently revoked-but-unexpired rows live for the full 30 days. Add an index on ExpiresAt to keep the delete cheap: e.HasIndex(x => x.ExpiresAt).

problem: TIER1/MEMORY LEAK — RedisDungeonCache's in-memory fallback dictionary only ever grows: entries expire logically (Expires check on read) but are never physically removed, and a Redis outage routes every dungeon definition (multi-KB JSON strings, one per run per floor) into this dictionary for the life of the process.
action: Evict expired fallback entries and bound the fallback's size.
location: services/backend/src/Aumbrye.Infrastructure/Caching/DungeonCache.cs (Lines 9-52 / RedisDungeonCache fallback; Lines 57-73 / InMemoryDungeonCache has the same unbounded growth)
implementation: Replace the hand-rolled ConcurrentDictionary with Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory.MemoryCache configured with SizeLimit (e.g. 256 MB, entry size = definitionJson.Length) and per-entry AbsoluteExpirationRelativeToNow = ttl; MemoryCache handles expiration scanning and LRU-style compaction natively. Apply the same to InMemoryDungeonCache (which production uses whenever Redis is not configured). Register MemoryCache via services.AddMemoryCache(o => o.SizeLimit = ...).

problem: TIER1/BUG — AffixRoller value rolling is inconsistent and crash-prone: (a) RollAffixValue's isFraction heuristic (tier.Max <= 1.0 && tier.Min >= 0 && tier.Max < 10) contains a redundant clause and misclassifies genuine fractional ranges like 1.2–2.4 into the integer branch, flooring/ceiling them into a different distribution than designed; (b) WeightedPick calls rng.NextInt(total) which THROWS ArgumentOutOfRangeException when every affix weight in the filtered pool is 0, killing the whole run-completion request.
action: Make value interpolation explicit per-affix instead of heuristic, and guard zero-weight pools.
implementation: 1) Add a bool IsPercent (or 'valueStyle': 'fraction'|'integer') field to AffixDefinition sourced from content/affixes JSON, and branch on it: fraction -> tier.Min + (tier.Max - tier.Min) * (rng.NextInt(10_000) / 10_000.0); integer -> rng.NextInt((int)tier.Min, (int)tier.Max + 1). 2) In WeightedPick: var total = pool.Sum(a => Math.Max(0, a.Weight)); if (total <= 0) return pool[0]; and clamp negative weights when accumulating. 3) Mirror the identical semantics in the GDScript affix roller so client-side rolls stay bit-identical with the backend (LOOT-4.1 determinism contract).

problem: TIER1/BUG — EnemyPlacer.PickWeighted throws when a biome's EnemyPool is empty or has all-zero weights (rng.NextInt(0) -> ArgumentOutOfRangeException), and the placer consumes RNG draws for entries it then discards over budget, which silently couples enemy determinism to the budget value — a tier/playerLevel change reshuffles ALL subsequent placements instead of only truncating them.
action: Guard degenerate pools and decouple the RNG stream from budget-dependent control flow.
implementation: 1) At method start: if (biome.EnemyPool.Count == 0 || biome.EnemyPool.Sum(e => e.Weight) <= 0) return ([], 0.0); 2) Restructure the loop to pre-roll the room's full candidate list from the rng regardless of budget (var picks = Enumerable.Range(0, maxPerRoom).Select(_ => PickWeighted(...)).ToList();) and then apply the budget filter over the pre-rolled list — the RNG consumption becomes a pure function of (seed, room count) so budget/tier tweaks no longer cascade into unrelated floors. Add a SeedReproducibility test asserting placements for tier N and N+1 share the same enemy id sequence prefix.

problem: TIER1/PERFORMANCE — CanonicalJsonSerializer.Serialize builds and serializes the entire canonical object graph TWICE per dungeon (once without checksum to hash, once with) — every generation attempt pays double allocation on a multi-KB payload that sits on the hot path of run creation and floor transitions.
action: Serialize once and inject the checksum without re-walking the object graph.
implementation: Because 'checksum' sorts deterministically in the SortedDictionary, serialize the checksum-less canonical form once, compute the SHA-256, then splice the checksum key into the existing root dictionary and serialize only the root again — or cheaper: since the canonical JSON is stable, build the final string with a single string insertion: json.Insert(json.LastIndexOf('}'), $",\"checksum\":\"{checksum}\"") is fragile; the robust minimal fix is to keep one BuildCanonicalObject call, serialize, hash, then root["checksum"] = checksum; var finalJson = JsonSerializer.Serialize(root, IndentedOptions); (reusing the same SortedDictionary instance instead of rebuilding the graph).

problem: TIER1/DESIGN DRIFT — Two parallel procgen implementations exist with an admitted authority split: DungeonGenerator.cs's own doc comment says 'GDScript DungeonProcgen is authoritative for gameplay; this path exists for backend/CLI parity', yet the C# path always emits empty RoomContent, Locks and Puzzles (Array.Empty) while the GDScript generator (apps/game/client/scripts/dungeon/procgen/room_content_assigner.gd, 926 lines) populates them. Server-issued definitions (USE_ONLINE_PROCgen path, checksum comparisons, procgen-cli baselines) therefore describe a different dungeon than the client plays, and any future flip to server-authoritative runs inherits a silent divergence.
action: Either port room-content/lock/puzzle assignment to the C# package or formally freeze the C# path to layout+placements-only with a versioned parity contract and tests that assert which fields are authoritative where.
location: packages/procedural/Generation/DungeonGenerator.cs (Lines 21-24 / authority comment; Lines 109-124 / DungeonDefinition construction with empty RoomContent/Locks/Puzzles) vs apps/game/client/scripts/dungeon/procgen/dungeon_procgen.gd and room_content_assigner.gd
implementation: Preferred (server-authoritative future): port room_content_assigner.gd, room_graph lock/key logic and puzzle assignment into packages/procedural/Assignment as pure functions of (biome, graph, SeededRandom) reusing the SplitMix64 stream discipline; extend ClientVersionParityTests to run both generators for a fixed seed matrix and diff canonical JSON field-by-field. Interim: add 'generatorCapabilities' to the definition JSON (e.g. ["layout","placements"]) so the client knows to run its own content pass on server definitions, and document the split in docs/ADR.

problem: TIER1/GDPR+CONSISTENCY — DeleteAccountAsync removes the Account row (cascading tokens/runs/save) but leaves the player's display name and accountId permanently readable on Redis/in-memory leaderboards, and ExportAccountAsync omits leaderboard entries from the data export. Deleted users remain publicly listed.
action: Purge leaderboard membership on account deletion and include leaderboard rows in the export.
implementation: Add Task RemoveAccountAsync(Guid accountId) to ILeaderboardStore. Redis implementation: SCAN keys matching leaderboard:*, and for each ZSCAN for members whose accountId prefix matches, ZREM them (with the one-member-per-account refactor this becomes a direct ZREM per known board; keep an index set account:{id}:boards written at submit time to avoid SCAN). Call it from DeleteAccountAsync before returning. In ExportAccountAsync add ["leaderboardEntries"] built from the same index. Add integration coverage in LeaderboardsIntegrationTests: submit, delete account, assert GET /leaderboards no longer contains the accountId.

problem: TIER1/ENHANCEMENT — SeededRandom.NextInt uses modulo reduction (NextULong() % max), introducing modulo bias for ranges that do not divide 2^64. Bias is tiny for gameplay ranges but this generator underpins the determinism contract shared with GDScript; any future range near 2^63 skews visibly, and the bias makes cross-language reimplementation subtly harder to verify.
action: Document the modulo reduction as part of the frozen cross-platform contract (preferred, since GDScript must match bit-for-bit), or switch both sides to Lemire's multiply-shift reduction simultaneously.
implementation: Do NOT change unilaterally — the GDScript twin must produce identical sequences. Option A (recommended): add a doc comment 'modulo reduction is intentional and contractually frozen; see seed determinism tests' and extend SeedReproducibilityTests with golden sequences (seed -> first 64 outputs for maxExclusive in {2,3,7,100,1000}) mirrored by a GDScript validation-suite test consuming the same golden file from content/fixtures. Option B: implement uint64 mulhi reduction ((UInt128)NextULong() * (uint)max >> 64) in both languages in the same release and regenerate goldens.

problem: TIER1/QUALITY — LeaderboardService uses run.CompletedAt - run.CreatedAt as the leaderboard time, which includes pause time, menu time, disconnections and floor-cache regeneration, while CompleteRunAsync separately validates a client-reported ElapsedSeconds that is then discarded. The two clocks routinely disagree by minutes, so the anti-cheat check (>5s to escape) and the ranked metric measure different things.
action: Pick one authoritative timing model: store the validated client elapsed on the Run row, cross-check it against the server wall-clock window, and rank by the stored value.
implementation: 1) Add double? ElapsedSeconds to the Run entity; in CompleteRunAsync after validation set run.ElapsedSeconds = input.ElapsedSeconds only if input.ElapsedSeconds <= (now - run.CreatedAt).TotalSeconds + 30 (client clock can never claim less wall time than actually passed minus skew; reject otherwise with 'Implausible elapsed time'). 2) LeaderboardService.SubmitFromRunAsync uses run.ElapsedSeconds ?? (CompletedAt - CreatedAt).TotalSeconds. 3) This preserves speedrun fairness (pause menus excluded client-side) while bounding manipulation to the wall-clock ceiling.

problem: TIER2/GAMEPLAY BUG — WeaponController's attack input buffer is dropped instead of chained. _try_attack stores _buffered_attack when pressed during an active swing (line 429), but the ONLY consumption site requires _post_dodge_attack_buffer > 0.0 (line 181), which is set exclusively by _on_dodge_ended. Result: pressing attack during recovery — the core combo-buffer pattern of every soulslike — does nothing unless a dodge just ended. This directly contradicts the 'snappy combat' design goal.
action: Consume the buffered attack whenever an attack ends, inside its own buffer window, independent of dodges.
implementation: 1) Add var _attack_buffer_timer := 0.0. In _try_attack when buffering: _buffered_attack = kind; _attack_buffer_timer = float(_weapon_data.get("buffer_window", 0.2)) + 0.1. 2) In _physics_process tick _attack_buffer_timer down and clear _buffered_attack at 0. 3) After the is_attacking checks (around line 181) replace the condition with: if _buffered_attack != "" and not is_attacking: var kind := _buffered_attack; _buffered_attack = ""; _try_attack(kind). Keep the post-dodge path as-is (it already re-buffers). 4) Verify in combat_suite.gd: simulate light press at recovery start, assert a second attack begins within one frame of _end_attack.

problem: TIER2/CRASH — WeaponController._ready dereferences _body without a null check: _body = get_parent() as CharacterBody3D returns null when the node is parented anywhere else (tool scenes, validation suites, accidental reparenting), and the very next line _body.get_node_or_null("Stamina") crashes with 'Attempt to call function on a null instance'.
action: Guard the parent cast and fail soft with a clear error.
implementation:
func _ready() -> void:
	_body = get_parent() as CharacterBody3D
	if _body == null:
		push_error("WeaponController must be a direct child of a CharacterBody3D (parent=%s)" % [get_parent()])
		set_physics_process(false)
		return
	... existing lookups ...
Also null-guard _connect_anim_hitbox_signals' _body usage (already guarded) and every has_method call on _body in helpers that can run before _ready completes.

problem: TIER2/CRITICAL GAMEPLAY BUG — Attack-token leak in CastleEnemyBase: _start_windup acquires a token from AttackTokenService (sets _attack_token_held = true), but the token is only released in _end_attack and begin_phase_transition. If the enemy is STAGGERED (apply_stagger jumps straight to State.STAGGER without _end_attack), DIES mid-windup/attack (_finalize_death never calls _release_attack_token), or is freed (_exit_tree has no release), the token stays checked out forever. Since tokens gate how many enemies may attack simultaneously, the pool drains over a session until NO enemy can ever attack again — a progressive, hard-to-reproduce combat freeze.
action: Release the attack token on every exit path from WINDUP/ATTACK: stagger, death, phase transition, tree exit.
location: apps/game/client/scripts/enemies/castle_enemy_base.gd (Lines 1322-1334 / _start_windup acquire; Lines 778-791 / apply_stagger; Lines 700-734 / _finalize_death; Lines 265-269 / _exit_tree; Lines 1475-1478 / _release_attack_token)
implementation: 1) In apply_stagger, before setting _state = State.STAGGER add: if _state in [State.WINDUP, State.ATTACK]: _combo_step = 0; _release_attack_token(). 2) In _finalize_death add _release_attack_token() next to _leave_room_engagement(). 3) In _exit_tree add _release_attack_token() before the room-board unregister. 4) Defensive: make AttackTokenService track holders by instance id (weakref) and reclaim tokens whose holder is no longer valid on a slow timer, logging a warning so future leak paths surface in playtests. 5) Add a lock_on/combat suite case: stagger an enemy mid-windup N times, then assert another enemy can still obtain a token.

problem: TIER2/BUG — Double hit-reaction per hit: CastleEnemyBase connects BOTH _hurtbox.damaged -> _on_hurt AND _hurtbox.hit_resolved -> _on_hit_resolved, and _on_hit_resolved manufactures a fresh empty DamageInfo and calls _on_hurt again. Hurtbox.receive_hit emits hit_resolved AND damaged for the same hit (hurtbox.gd lines 158-159), so every successful hit plays the flinch/tween twice in one frame and _last_hit_direction is clobbered by the empty DamageInfo's zero direction, breaking directional death sweeps.
action: Route reaction handling through exactly one signal; keep hit_resolved only for zero-damage bookkeeping if needed.
location: apps/game/client/scripts/enemies/castle_enemy_base.gd (Lines 240-243 / signal connection in _ready; Lines 1532-1535 / _on_hit_resolved; Lines 1538-1550 / _on_hurt) and apps/game/client/scripts/combat/hurtbox.gd (Lines 158-159 / dual emission)
implementation: Delete the _on_hit_resolved -> _on_hurt forwarding: either (a) remove the hit_resolved connection entirely and rely on damaged, or (b) keep hit_resolved as the single source: connect only hit_resolved, and inside it read res.outgoing > 0.0 before playing flinch, passing the ORIGINAL info.direction by extending DamageResolution with a direction field populated in Hurtbox.receive_hit (res.direction = info.direction) so _last_hit_direction stays correct. Option (b) is cleaner because blocked/dodged hits then skip the flinch naturally.

problem: TIER2/BUG — set_catalog_id reconfigures poise with a single argument (_poise.configure(_data.get("poise", 40.0))) while every other call site passes (poise, stagger_duration). If Poise.configure has no default for the second parameter this is a runtime error on every spawned add (spawn_adds -> set_catalog_id path); if it has a default, the enemy's stagger duration silently resets to the default instead of the catalog value — either way boss adds behave differently from directly-placed enemies of the same id.
action: Pass the full tuning tuple on the catalog-override path.
implementation: Replace with: if _poise and not _data.is_empty(): _poise.configure(float(_data.get("poise", 40.0)), float(_data.get("stagger_duration", 1.0))). Note _unpack_tuning() is already called two lines later and sets _stagger_duration_data, so the cleanest fix is to reorder: set _data, call _unpack_tuning() FIRST, then configure health/poise from the unpacked fields — removing the duplicated literal defaults entirely.

problem: TIER2/BUG — Hurtbox hyperarmor misreporting and DoT visual spam: (a) when hyperarmor is active the poise hit is scaled by 0.25 and reported in res.poise_outgoing but _poise.take_poise_damage is never called, so telemetry/HUD sees poise damage that was never applied; (b) _emit_victim_feedback fires play_blood_decal AND play_impact_decal on EVERY damaging hit including each periodic status tick (receive_periodic_damage routes through receive_hit), so a 10-tick poison stack spawns 20 decals plus material flashes — measurable frame cost in group fights.
action: Zero out unapplied poise in the resolution, and suppress heavy VFX for periodic ticks.
location: apps/game/client/scripts/combat/hurtbox.gd (Lines 137-149 / hyperarmor poise branch; Lines 318-368 / _emit_victim_feedback; Lines 180-186 / receive_periodic_damage)
implementation: 1) In the poise block: if hyperarmor: res.absorbed_by_poise = true; res.poise_outgoing = 0.0 (or apply the reduced hit: _poise.take_poise_damage(poise_hit) with the 0.25 multiplier — pick the intended design and make the report match; soulslike convention applies reduced poise damage through hyperarmor, so prefer applying it). 2) Thread info.periodic into feedback: in _emit_victim_feedback add an early branch — if periodic, only run the material flash at 0.3 strength and skip both decal calls and HitFeedback camera shake. Pass info into _emit_victim_feedback instead of the current six positional args to stop the signature from growing.

problem: TIER2/BUG — Endless-mode skip items are consumed before floor generation is attempted. start_endless_run calls SkipFloorSvc.consume_skip(...) up front; if _start_mode_run's _generate_dungeon then fails, the flow returns to hub with an error and the (rare, milestone-reward) skip item is permanently gone with no floor gained.
action: Consume the skip item only after generation succeeds, or refund it on the failure path.
implementation: Restructure: read start_floor = SkipFloorSvc.start_floor_for_item(skip_item_id) WITHOUT consuming; stash var _pending_skip_item := skip_item_id; consume inside _enter_run() (the success path) via SkipFloorSvc.consume_skip; clear _pending_skip_item on the generation-failure branch before return_to_hub. Alternatively keep the early consume but in the failure branch call InventoryService.add_loot(_pending_skip_item) to refund, emitting a run_warning('Floor skip refunded'). Add a flow_suite case using _test_resolve_floor_override = [] to force failure and assert inventory still contains the skip item.

problem: TIER2/BUG — _submit_leaderboard_async unlocks the 'leaderboard_submit' achievement unconditionally, even when the HTTP submit failed or the player was offline; and complete_run_via_portal sets root meta 'run_results' twice in a row (lines 577 and 580) — dead duplicate that suggests a lost edit between them (_clear_in_run_meta and _handle_escape_meta run between the two writes).
action: Gate the achievement on a successful submit and delete the redundant meta write.
implementation: In _submit_leaderboard_async: if AchievementService and lb.get("ok", false) and lb.get("body", {}).get("submitted", false): AchievementService.unlock("leaderboard_submit"). In complete_run_via_portal remove the second get_tree().root.set_meta("run_results", last_run_results) at line 580 (the first at 577 already precedes _clear_in_run_meta — verify _clear_in_run_meta does not erase 'run_results'; if it does, keep ONLY the second write and delete the first, and add a comment stating the ordering constraint).

problem: TIER2/CROSS-STACK CONTRACT DRIFT — ApiClient.complete_run never sends the 'floor' field, but the backend CompleteRunRequest carries req.Floor and uses it to select which floor's definition validates loot claims (RunService.CompleteRunAsync completedFloor). A multi-floor castle/endless run completed via the cloud path therefore always validates against floor 1, guaranteeing 'Unknown loot instance id' rejections for floors 2+ once online runs are enabled. Client retry-on-timeout for this non-idempotent POST can also double-complete.
action: Send the completed floor in the payload, and stop retrying non-idempotent POSTs (or add an idempotency key).
location: apps/game/client/scripts/net/api_client.gd (Lines 130-143 / complete_run payload; Lines 232-248 / _request_json retry loop) vs services/backend/src/Aumbrye.Api/Endpoints/ApiEndpoints.cs (Lines 160-179 / CompleteRun binding)
implementation: 1) Extend complete_run(run_id, outcome, elapsed, boss_defeated, loot_claimed_ids, floor := 1) and include "floor": floor in the payload; RunFlow._cloud_finalize_run passes RunFlow.current_floor. 2) In _request_json, add an is_idempotent parameter (GET/PUT true, POST false by default); only retry when idempotent OR when the request carries an Idempotency-Key header the server honors. 3) Backend: accept an optional Idempotency-Key on /runs and /complete, caching the first response per key for 24h (a small table keyed by accountId+key). This closes both the duplicate-run and duplicate-completion windows in one design.

problem: TIER2/SECURITY — The persisted session file (refresh token + account id + email) is encrypted with OS.get_unique_id() as the password. That value is a stable, low-entropy machine identifier readable by any local process, is documented to return an empty string on some platforms (making the file effectively plaintext), and never changes — so one leaked session.json is decryptable by anyone who knows the scheme.
action: Derive the session-file key from a per-install random secret stored via the platform keychain where available, with an explicit fallback and threat-model comment.
implementation: 1) Generate a random 32-byte install secret on first boot (Crypto.new().generate_random_bytes(32)), store it hex-encoded in user://install_key with best-effort obfuscation, and derive the pass as install_secret + OS.get_unique_id() so both the file AND the machine are needed. 2) If OS.get_unique_id() == "", still function (secret alone). 3) On decrypt failure, silently treat as signed-out (already the behavior via load_session returning false). 4) Long term: move refresh tokens to Steam Auth session tickets on Steam builds so no long-lived secret rests on disk. Note the residual risk in a comment: local malware can always steal what the game itself can read; the goal is raising the bar from 'copy one file' to 'copy two files + know the scheme'.

problem: TIER2/BUGS — Leaderboard fetch path: fetch_leaderboard demands an authenticated session (await require_session()) although GET /api/v1/leaderboards is a public endpoint server-side, blocking signed-out players from viewing boards in-game; and biome_id is interpolated into the query string without URL-encoding, so any future biome id containing '&' or spaces silently corrupts the request.
action: Drop the session requirement for the public read and encode query parameters.
implementation:
static func fetch_leaderboard(biome_id: String, tier: int, limit: int = 10) -> Dictionary:
	var url := _build_url(LEADERBOARDS) + "?biomeId=%s&tier=%d&limit=%d" % [biome_id.uri_encode(), tier, limit]
	return await _request_json(url, HTTPClient.METHOD_GET, {}, false)
(auth=false sends only the version headers, which the public policy accepts). Keep require_session solely on submit_leaderboard.

problem: TIER2/DATA BUG — Steam Cloud save adoption compares timestamps as raw strings across different clocks: cloudUpdatedAt written by the backend is an ISO-8601 UTC instant, while local saves stamp Time.get_datetime_string_from_system() (LOCAL time, no offset suffix). The lexicographic '<=' comparison in _try_adopt_steam_cloud_save can therefore prefer an older save for any user whose timezone is ahead of UTC, silently discarding hours of progress on a fresh install with Steam Cloud enabled.
action: Normalize every save timestamp to UTC ISO-8601 at write time and compare parsed unix times, not strings.
implementation: 1) Introduce a helper: static func _utc_now_iso() -> String: return Time.get_datetime_string_from_system(true) (utc=true) + "Z" and use it for savedAt/roster stamps. 2) In the adoption check parse both sides: var cloud_unix := Time.get_unix_time_from_datetime_string(cloud_updated); var local_unix := Time.get_unix_time_from_datetime_string(local_updated); adopt only when cloud_unix > local_unix; treat parse failures (0) as 'unknown' and prefer the LOCAL save with a push_warning. 3) SaveMigrator: add a migration step normalizing legacy local-time stamps by appending no suffix but flagging them so comparisons treat them as untrusted.

problem: TIER2/DATA BUG — Save writes can fail silently: _write_save returns false on open failure, read-back validation failure, or rename failure, but autosave() ignores the return value and no user-facing signal fires. A player whose disk is full or whose antivirus locks the file plays for hours believing progress is saved; save_failed is only emitted on LOAD problems.
action: Propagate write failures to the save_failed signal and surface a HUD toast, with a retry.
implementation: 1) Change autosave to: var ok := _write_save(_build_save_payload(), true, priority); if not ok: save_failed.emit("write_failed"); and add one retry after 1s via get_tree().create_timer before emitting. 2) In the UI layer (combat_hud or hub), connect LocalSave.save_failed to a non-blocking toast: 'Saving failed — check disk space'. 3) In _write_save, when the IMMEDIATE read-back validation fails, log WHICH validator problem occurred (join SaveValidator.validate(verified)) so corruption sources are diagnosable instead of the current silent temp-file delete.

problem: TIER2/CRASH VECTOR — dungeon_builder.gd contains 23 'await get_tree()...' suspension points inside its chunked build pipeline. If the player exits to hub / dies during a floor build (scene change frees the builder's nodes), resumed coroutines execute against freed instances — the classic Godot 'previously freed instance' crash, intermittent and build-machine dependent. castle_run.gd (3 awaits) and loading_screen share the pattern.
action: Guard every post-await continuation with is_inside_tree()/is_instance_valid checks, and make the build cancellable via a generation token.
location: apps/game/client/scripts/dungeon/dungeon_builder.gd (23 await sites across the chunked build methods) and apps/game/client/scripts/dungeon/castle_run.gd (3 await sites)
implementation: 1) Add a monotonically increasing build id: var _build_generation := 0; each build_floor call captures var my_gen := _build_generation (incremented at entry and in a cancel() called from _exit_tree). 2) After EVERY await insert: if my_gen != _build_generation or not is_inside_tree(): return. 3) For awaits on external nodes (BiomeRegistry prewarm), re-validate fetched node references after resumption with is_instance_valid before dereferencing. 4) Add a dungeon_suite test that starts a build, frees the builder one frame later, and pumps 120 frames asserting no script error is pushed (use CrashLogger hook or Engine error capture).

problem: TIER2/PERF+CORRECTNESS — Enemy line-of-sight raycasts hardcode collision_mask = 1, so any occluder authored on a different physics layer (doors, procedural dressing, boss-arena gates) is invisible to enemy perception — enemies aggro and shoot through geometry that blocks the player. The same hardcoded mask appears in the LOS cache path used by deaggro, meaning cover mechanics silently depend on every wall being on layer 1.
action: Source the occlusion mask from a single project-level constant/export and audit dungeon geometry layers against it.
implementation: 1) Create a CombatLayers helper (scripts/combat/combat_layers.gd) with const WORLD_OCCLUDERS := 0b1 | (1 << 4) (match project.godot layer names for 'world' and 'doors'). 2) params.collision_mask = CombatLayers.WORLD_OCCLUDERS. 3) Add an export override @export_flags_3d_physics var los_mask := CombatLayers.WORLD_OCCLUDERS for special enemies. 4) Extend dungeon_suite: spawn an enemy behind a door mesh on the door layer and assert _has_line_of_sight_to_player() is false.

problem: TIER2/BLOAT — ~15,000 lines of validation suites (validation/suites/*.gd, 25+ files up to 1442 lines each), diagnostic tools (scripts/tools/_diag_keys.gd, _diag_settings.gd — currently staged in git), and procgen_seed_health.gd ship inside the client scripts tree. They are exported into release builds (bigger PCK, longer script compile at boot) and expand the cheat/attack surface since suites contain state-manipulation helpers.
action: Exclude validation/diagnostic code from release exports and relocate it under a dev-only path.
implementation: 1) Move validation/ and tools/_diag_* to apps/game/client/dev/ (updating res:// references in validation_runner.gd and any autoload/scene that mentions them — grep for 'validation/suites'). 2) In export_presets.cfg add exclude filters to every release preset: exclude_filter="dev/*,scripts/tools/_diag_*". 3) Guard the runner entry point with OS.is_debug_build() so a stray inclusion is inert. 4) Un-stage the two _diag .uid files (git restore --staged apps/game/client/scripts/tools/_diag_*.uid) or commit them under the new dev/ path.

problem: TIER2/BUG — Bow state machine desyncs HUD/animation listeners: entering DRAWING sets is_attacking = true without emitting attack_started, and _reset_bow (cancelled draw) clears state without emitting attack_ended, while _fire_bow_shot emits attack_started for a swing whose attack_ended arrives later via _end_attack. Any listener pairing started/ended events (combat HUD stamina lock, anim director, audio ducking) sees mismatched pairs on bows. Additionally the DRAWING phase never suppresses stamina regen, but _end_attack after a shot resets regen to NORMAL — harmless today but asymmetric.
action: Emit a consistent signal pair for the draw cycle and make regen state changes symmetric.
implementation: 1) When entering DRAWING (line 783-787) emit attack_started.emit("bow_draw") and call _stamina.set_regen_state(Stamina.RegenState.SUPPRESSED). 2) In _reset_bow emit attack_ended.emit() and restore regen NORMAL. 3) _fire_bow_shot: do not re-emit attack_started (the draw already did) OR emit a dedicated signal bow_released(charge) that the anim director consumes; pick one and update combat_hud.gd listeners accordingly. 4) Add combat_suite coverage: press-hold heavy, release below threshold, assert attack_started/attack_ended counts are equal.

problem: TIER2/DESIGN — RunFlow._cloud_finalize_run is intentionally fire-and-forget (calls the async variant without await), so complete_run + push_to_cloud race the RESULTS_SCENE transition and any app quit. A player who closes the game on the results screen loses the server-side completion, and because the client already cleared the local active run, the server-side run stays 'Active' forever (also blocking leaderboard submission which requires Completed status).
action: Persist an outbox of unfinalized cloud completions and replay it on next boot.
implementation: 1) Before firing, append {runId, outcome, elapsed, bossDefeated, lootIds, attempts:0} to a 'cloudOutbox' array in LocalSave meta and autosave. 2) On successful complete_run + push, remove the entry. 3) In ApiConfig._ready (or a small CloudOutbox autoload) after session refresh, replay pending entries with attempts++ and drop after 5 failures. 4) Keep the fire-and-forget UX (no blocking), since the outbox guarantees eventual delivery. This also absorbs the retry-idempotency work from the api_client change (send the same Idempotency-Key from the outbox entry).

problem: TIER2/QUALITY — DungeonBuilder's floor cache is a static Dictionary keyed by floor index, trimmed only relative to the current floor and fully cleared at run boundaries. store_floor_cache(current_floor, definition, current_floor) passes the same value for floor and reference_floor (suspicious API), and because the cache is static, a crash-abandoned run's definitions survive into the next run until clear_floor_cache happens to be called — a stale-definition hazard for seeded/challenge runs where two runs share floor indices.
action: Namespace the floor cache by run identity so stale entries cannot leak across runs.
location: apps/game/client/scripts/dungeon/dungeon_builder.gd (Lines 70-103 / store_floor_cache, get_floor_cache, clear_floor_cache, _trim_floor_cache) and apps/game/client/scripts/app/run_flow.gd (Lines 1009-1022 / cache accessors)
implementation: 1) Add a static var _cache_run_key := "" set via DungeonBuilder.begin_run_cache(run_key) where run_key = "%s:%d:%s" % [run_mode, seed, run_id]; store entries as {run_key, floor -> definition} and have get_floor_cache return {} when run_key differs. 2) RunFlow calls begin_run_cache in _start_mode_run and _restore_castle_run (replacing _clear_floor_cache). 3) Collapse the double-floor parameter: store_floor_cache(floor_index, definition) with trim referencing an internally tracked current floor set by a separate set_reference_floor(floor) call from RunFlow.

problem: TIER3/SECURITY — The web app stores the refresh token in sessionStorage, which any XSS payload can exfiltrate for a 30-day account takeover (rotation helps but the stolen token wins the race). sessionStorage also kills sessions on every new tab, forcing re-login and making the 'remember me' experience impossible without downgrading to localStorage (worse).
action: Move web refresh tokens to an httpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie issued by the backend; keep the access token in memory only.
location: apps/web/src/auth/AuthProvider.tsx (Lines 29-48 / storeRefreshToken, scheduleRefresh; Lines 83-109 / refreshSession) and services/backend/src/Aumbrye.Api/Endpoints/ApiEndpoints.cs (Lines 20-57 / register/login/refresh endpoints)
implementation: Backend: add a cookie mode negotiated via a 'X-Auth-Transport: cookie' request header — on login/register/refresh, when present, Set-Cookie: aumbrye_rt=<token>; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v1/auth; Max-Age=2592000 and omit refreshToken from the JSON body; /refresh reads the cookie when the body token is absent; /logout clears it. CORS already sends credentials (AllowCredentials is set). Web: delete storeRefreshToken/sessionStorage usage; refresh() posts {} with credentials:'include'; keep the in-memory access token and the pre-expiry timer as-is. Game client (Godot) continues using body tokens — the header opt-in keeps both contracts on one endpoint.

problem: TIER3/BUG — Infinite reload loop on version mismatch: VersionGate auto-reloads once per module load (module-scope reloadAttempted), but a full page reload resets module state. If the server keeps returning 426 (user's cached bundle is genuinely stale AND the CDN keeps serving it, or the server's expected version is misconfigured), every login attempt triggers another automatic reload — an endless reload cycle that never shows the manual UI.
action: Persist the auto-reload attempt across reloads and only auto-reload once per version incident.
location: apps/web/src/components/VersionGate.tsx (Lines 4-16 / reloadAttempted guard and auto-reload effect)
implementation: useEffect(() => { if (!versionMismatch) return; const key = 'aumbrye_reload_attempted'; if (sessionStorage.getItem(key)) return; sessionStorage.setItem(key, String(Date.now())); window.location.reload(); }, [versionMismatch]); and clear the key on successful app boot (e.g. in main.tsx after first successful health/auth call: sessionStorage.removeItem('aumbrye_reload_attempted')). The manual Reload button stays. Optionally append a cache-busting query (?v=Date.now()) on the automatic reload to punch through stale CDN HTML.

problem: TIER3/BUG — Leaderboards page trusts URL parameters: tier = Number(searchParams.get('tier') ?? '1') produces NaN for ?tier=abc and any integer for ?tier=999, sending an invalid query the API answers for tier 999 with an empty board (and 'tier=NaN' serializes as literal NaN in the querystring, a guaranteed 400). The select then renders with a value matching no option.
action: Clamp and validate the tier (and biomeId) read from the URL before querying.
implementation: const rawTier = Number(searchParams.get('tier') ?? '1'); const tier = Number.isInteger(rawTier) ? Math.min(10, Math.max(1, rawTier)) : 1; const biomeIds = new Set(biomes.map(b => b.id)); const requested = searchParams.get('biomeId'); const biomeId = requested && biomeIds.has(requested) ? requested : (biomes[0]?.id ?? 'forgotten_castle'); Optionally normalize the URL once via setSearchParams(..., { replace: true }) when the parsed values differ from the raw params so shared links are canonical.

problem: TIER3/BUG — The web API client's timeout silently disappears when a caller supplies its own AbortSignal: request() uses init.signal ?? controller.signal, so every react-query call (which always passes signal) has NO timeout — a hung backend leaves queries pending until the browser gives up, and the AbortController+setTimeout pair still runs pointlessly.
action: Combine the caller's signal with the timeout signal instead of choosing one.
implementation: Use AbortSignal.any (supported in evergreen browsers; polyfill fallback below): const signals = [controller.signal, ...(init.signal ? [init.signal] : [])]; const signal = 'any' in AbortSignal ? AbortSignal.any(signals) : controller.signal; fetch(url, { ...init, signal, ... }). Fallback without .any: init.signal?.addEventListener('abort', () => controller.abort(), { once: true }); and always pass controller.signal to fetch. Keep clearTimeout in finally as-is.

problem: TIER3/BLOAT — gray-matter (plus its js-yaml dependency and a Buffer polyfill shipped to every visitor) is bundled solely to split '---' frontmatter from a handful of local wiki/patch-note markdown files whose frontmatter the project fully controls. That is roughly 70-100 KB of vendored parser + polyfill for a task 20 lines of code covers, and the Buffer global pollutes the page for all code.
action: Replace gray-matter with a minimal built-in frontmatter parser and delete the Buffer polyfill.
location: apps/web/src/content/loader.ts (Lines 1-50 / matter usage) and apps/web/src/polyfills.ts (entire file) and apps/web/src/main.tsx (polyfill import)
implementation:
function parseFrontmatter(raw: string): { data: Record<string,string|string[]>, content: string } { const m = /^---?
([\s\S]*?)?
---?
?/.exec(raw); if (!m) return { data: {}, content: raw }; const data: Record<string, any> = {}; for (const line of m[1].split(/?
/)) { const kv = /^(\w[\w-]*):\s*(.*)$/.exec(line); if (!kv) continue; data[kv[1]] = kv[2].startsWith('[') ? kv[2].slice(1,-1).split(',').map(s => s.trim().replace(/^"|"$/g,'')) : kv[2].replace(/^"|"$/g,''); } return { data, content: raw.slice(m[0].length) }; } Then constrain your frontmatter authoring to scalars + inline arrays (already true for highlights), swap matter(raw) calls, remove gray-matter and buffer from package.json, delete polyfills.ts and its import.

problem: TIER3/CONTRACT DRIFT — apps/web/src/api/schema.d.ts is a hand-maintained 192-line snapshot of the backend OpenAPI surface. Any backend change (e.g. adding 'floor' to CompleteRunRequest, cookie-mode auth, new problem fields) silently drifts from these types; scripts/openapi-drift exists but nothing forces it in the loop.
action: Generate schema.d.ts from the served OpenAPI document in CI and fail the build on drift.
implementation: 1) Add an npm script: "gen:api": "openapi-typescript http://localhost:8080/swagger/v1/swagger.json -o src/api/schema.d.ts" (or point at a checked-in swagger.json exported by the backend's OpenApiContractTests). 2) CI job: boot the API in Testing mode (UseInMemoryStores), run gen:api into a temp file, diff against the committed schema.d.ts, exit non-zero on mismatch with the message 'run npm run gen:api'. 3) Wire the same swagger.json snapshot into scripts/openapi-drift so backend and web validate against one artifact.

problem: TIER3/CONTENT — Schema versioning debris: content/schemas ships v1 AND v2 for biome-definition, character-state, dungeon-definition and inventory with no manifest declaring which version each consumer pins. Backend CharacterStateDefaults writes schemaVersion:1 saves while the client SaveMigrator.CURRENT_VERSION is far ahead (client save payloads carry their own higher version), and dungeon-definition.v1 no longer matches the C# serializer output shape used at runtime. Stale schemas invite validators (scripts/validate-content) to bless content the engine can no longer load.
action: Author a schema manifest mapping consumer -> pinned schema version, migrate remaining v1 references, and delete or quarantine superseded schemas.
location: content/schemas/biome-definition.v1.json, character-state.v1.json, character-state.v2.json, dungeon-definition.v1.json, dungeon-definition.v2.json, inventory.v1.json, inventory.v2.json (and services/backend/src/Aumbrye.Application/Services/CharacterStateService.cs Lines 11-47 / schemaVersion:1 default state)
implementation: 1) Add content/schemas/MANIFEST.json: { "dungeon-definition": { "current": "v2", "consumers": ["backend:CanonicalJsonSerializer", "client:dungeon_builder"] }, ... }. 2) Make scripts/validate-content read the manifest and validate every content file against ONLY its current schema, erroring if a file self-declares a retired version. 3) Move retired schemas to content/schemas/retired/ kept solely for SaveMigrator reference. 4) Reconcile the backend: CharacterStateDefaults must emit the same schemaVersion the client SaveMigrator considers current (read the constant from a shared fixture consumed by ClientVersionParityTests so backend/client cannot diverge silently).

problem: REPO/BLOAT — Repository root carries generated/scratch artifacts: project_structure.txt (1 MB dump), get_all_file_names.py (the script that produced it), .pytest_cache/, .ruff_cache/, tools/__pycache__/, and bin/obj build output directories are present in the tree (obj files surfaced by file search). These inflate clones, pollute searches, and the staged _diag .uid files indicate debug tooling was about to be committed.
action: Delete scratch artifacts, extend .gitignore, and untrack build/cache directories.
location: Repository root (project_structure.txt, get_all_file_names.py, .pytest_cache/, .ruff_cache/, tools/__pycache__/; services/backend/**/obj, packages/**/obj per Glob results; staged apps/game/client/scripts/tools/_diag_*.gd.uid per git status)
implementation: 1) git rm --cached -r any tracked obj/ bin/ __pycache__ .pytest_cache .ruff_cache entries; delete project_structure.txt and get_all_file_names.py (regenerate on demand with 'git ls-files'). 2) Append to .gitignore: **/obj/, **/bin/, __pycache__/, .pytest_cache/, .ruff_cache/, project_structure.txt. 3) Decide the fate of the staged _diag tool uids together with the dev-directory relocation entry above (either commit under dev/ or unstage). 4) Add a CI lint step that fails when files matching those patterns appear in a diff.

problem: TIER2/UX BUG — get_current_objective formats the waves objective with tr("PAUSE_OBJECTIVE_WAVES") % WavesRunService.current_wave. If any locale's translation omits or malforms the '%d' placeholder, the % operation raises a runtime error in the pause menu for that locale only — a crash class that testing in English never catches.
action: Guard translated format strings before interpolation.
implementation: Add a small helper: func _tr_fmt(key: String, args: Array) -> String: var s := tr(key); if s.count("%") == 0: return s; if s.count("%s") + s.count("%d") != args.size(): push_warning("Bad placeholder count in %s" % key); return s; return s % args — and use _tr_fmt("PAUSE_OBJECTIVE_WAVES", [WavesRunService.current_wave]). Additionally add a translations lint script (scripts/tools) that walks every .po/.csv entry containing % and verifies placeholder parity against the source string; run it in CI.

problem: TIER1/ROBUSTNESS — VersionHeaderMiddleware hand-writes ProblemDetails and hardcodes httpstatuses.com URLs, duplicating what AddProblemDetails already provides; more importantly it enforces the version gate on /api/v1/health too, which container orchestration probes may call with stale headers after a deploy, flapping health checks during rollouts.
action: Exempt health endpoints from version gating and emit problems through the standard writer.
implementation: 1) Early-return before the version checks when context.Request.Path.StartsWithSegments("/api/v1/health"). 2) Replace WriteProblemAsync with IProblemDetailsService: inject via constructor (RequestDelegate next, IProblemDetailsService problems) and call await problems.WriteAsync(new ProblemDetailsContext { HttpContext = context, ProblemDetails = new ProblemDetails { Status = statusCode, Title = ..., Detail = detail } }); which honors content negotiation and the app's customizations. 3) Keep 426 for client version and consider 428/400 consistency documented in the OpenAPI description.

problem: TIER1/ENHANCEMENT — Registration accepts near-arbitrary emails (only checks Contains('@') and length) and both register and login leak account existence: register returns 'Email already registered.' and login short-circuits password verification when the account is missing, creating a measurable timing difference for user enumeration.
action: Tighten email validation, equalize login timing, and make the register-conflict response enumeration-safe within product constraints.
implementation: 1) Validate with System.Net.Mail.MailAddress.TryCreate(email, out var addr) && addr.Address == email plus the existing length cap. 2) In LoginAsync always burn a hash: if (account == null) { _passwordHasher.Verify(password, DummyBcryptHash); return invalid; } where DummyBcryptHash is a precomputed hash of a random constant at the same work factor (11). 3) For register, either keep the explicit message (acceptable for a game) but rate-limit it separately at 5/min/IP, or switch to the email-verification pattern ('If this address is new, you will receive...') if email infrastructure lands later. Document the chosen posture in an ADR.

problem: TIER2/PERF — CastleEnemyBase._broadcast_alert and _alert_candidates fall back to get_tree().get_nodes_in_group("enemy") (a whole-floor scan) whenever the room board is empty, and WeaponController._find_soft_lock_target plus _resolve_backstab_target iterate every 'lockable'/'enemy' group member per attack press. With endless-mode floors holding many rooms of enemies these O(N) scans run inside single frames alongside per-enemy physics; there is no spatial partition anywhere in the combat query path.
action: Route proximity queries through the existing EnemyBlackboard room rosters and add a cheap distance prefilter service.
implementation: 1) Give EnemyBlackboard a static func nearby(origin: Vector3, radius: float) -> Array that iterates only rooms whose registered AABB intersects the radius (rooms already have ids; cache a center/extent per room at registration). 2) _alert_candidates returns EnemyBlackboard.nearby(global_position, _alert_radius) with the group scan kept only as a debug fallback behind OS.is_debug_build(). 3) WeaponController queries EnemyBlackboard.nearby(_body.global_position, SOFT_LOCK_RANGE) instead of the scene group; enemies register/unregister in the lockable index from _ready/_exit_tree. 4) Profile before/after with 60 enemies via the m6 suite to confirm the win.

problem: FUTURE/ROADMAP — Server-authoritative runs are stubbed but disabled: RunFlow.USE_ONLINE_PROCgen is hardcoded false ('Intentionally off pending server-authoritative runs'), the client generates and self-reports everything (kills, boss flags, loot ids), and the backend accepts completion claims constrained only by loot-id membership and elapsed bounds. action: Define and implement the online-run milestone: definition download per floor, server-verified completion, and offline fallback with clear integrity labeling.
location: apps/game/client/scripts/app/run_flow.gd (Lines 28-29 / USE_ONLINE_PROCgen const; Lines 316-349 / _generate_dungeon and _try_online_generate) and services/backend/src/Aumbrye.Application/Services/RunService.cs (whole service)
implementation: Milestone plan: 1) Land the Tier-1 fixes for multi-floor loot union, floor clamping, idempotent completion, and the Tier-2 'floor' payload field — these are prerequisites. 2) Add GET /runs/{id}/dungeon?floor=N usage in _resolve_floor_definition when online (cache locally per floor, fall back to LocalProcgen with a definition-checksum comparison logged as telemetry to quantify parity drift in the wild). 3) Mark each run record with generator provenance (server|local) and only server-generated runs become leaderboard-eligible (LeaderboardService checks run.DefinitionChecksum != null && run.GeneratorKind == Server). 4) Client UI: show a 'ranked' badge only for eligible runs, so offline play stays first-class without polluting boards.

problem: FUTURE/ROADMAP — OAuth (Google/Discord) is explicitly deferred ('deferred to post-EA — see known issues' hardcoded in the Account page) and password auth has no email verification or reset flow: a forgotten password is unrecoverable account loss, which for a live game with cloud saves is a support incident generator.
action: Prioritize a password-reset flow before broad EA, then layer OAuth providers on the existing token pipeline.
location: apps/web/src/pages/Account.tsx (Line 167 / deferred-OAuth notice) and services/backend/src/Aumbrye.Application/Services/AuthService.cs (no reset/verification surface exists)
implementation: Phase 1 (reset): add PasswordResetToken entity (accountId, tokenHash SHA-256, ExpiresAt 30min, UsedAt); POST /auth/forgot (always 204, rate-limited 3/hour/IP) emails a one-time link; POST /auth/reset {token,newPassword} verifies, rehashes with BCrypt(11), revokes ALL refresh-token families for the account. Needs a mail sender abstraction (IEmailSender) with a console implementation for dev. Phase 2 (OAuth): add /auth/oauth/{provider} using the authorization-code flow server-side; on first sign-in link by verified email when one matches, otherwise create an account with Email null like the Steam path; reuse IssueTokensAsync unchanged. Web: add 'Forgot password' + provider buttons; keep the Godot client on Steam auth.

problem: TIER2/QUALITY — respawn_at_rest/apply_state resurrect enemies with full patrol AI but never re-enable _body_collision when the enemy previously died silently: _finalize_death sets _body_collision.disabled = true, while respawn_at_rest restores hurtbox monitoring, HP bar, animator and dissolve visuals yet leaves the body collider disabled — a bonfire-respawned enemy is a ghost the player (and its own navigation) walks through.

Audit apply_state's revive path too — it delegates to respawn_at_rest, so the single fix covers both, but add a dungeon_suite assertion: kill an enemy, rest at bonfire, then cast a physics ray at the enemy and assert it reports a hit on the body layer.

location: apps/game/client/scripts/app/run_flow.gd (Lines 1100-1118 / restart_current_floor; Lines 658-663 / register_kill; Lines 1025-1031 / register_loot)

problem: TIER2/BUG (AUDIO) — AudioDirector.set_biome computes layer frequencies in the wrong order: _combat_freq = float(_profile.get("combatFreq", _music_freq)) executes BEFORE _music_freq is updated from the new profile's bossFreq. Any biome audio profile that omits combatFreq inherits the PREVIOUS biome's boss frequency, so the procedural combat layer plays the wrong pitch after every biome transition (endless mode changes biome per region) until a profile with an explicit combatFreq resets it.
action: Reorder the assignments so all fallback sources are refreshed before dependents read them.
implementation: Reorder to: _ambience_freq = float(_profile.get("ambienceFreq", 110.0)); _music_freq = float(_profile.get("bossFreq", 196.0)); _explore_freq = float(_profile.get("exploreFreq", _ambience_freq)); _combat_freq = float(_profile.get("combatFreq", _music_freq)); then the four set_meta calls. Add an audio_suite case: load biome A (bossFreq 300, no combatFreq), then biome B (bossFreq 196, no combatFreq), assert _combat_freq == 196 not 300.

problem: TIER2/CRASH VECTOR (UI) — InventoryUI connects an anonymous lambda to SceneTree.scene_changed (get_tree().scene_changed.connect(func(): call_deferred("_bind_inventory_context"))). The SceneTree outlives the UI node, and a lambda Callable is NOT auto-disconnected when the capturing node is freed (only bound-method callables are). After the inventory UI is freed on a scene swap, the next scene change invokes the stale lambda, which calls call_deferred on a freed instance — an intermittent 'previously freed instance' error that fires on every subsequent scene transition for the rest of the session.
action: Use a bound method (auto-disconnects with the node) or CONNECT_ONE_SHOT/explicit disconnect in _exit_tree.
implementation: Replace with a real method: get_tree().scene_changed.connect(_on_scene_changed) and func _on_scene_changed() -> void: call_deferred("_bind_inventory_context") — bound-method callables are cleaned up automatically when the object is freed, eliminating the stale connection. Sweep the codebase for the same pattern with: grep -rn "connect(func" apps/game/client/scripts and fix every connection whose signal owner (SceneTree, autoloads, servers) outlives the connecting node the same way.

problem: TIER2/BUG (VFX) — Engine.time_scale hitstop can strand the game in slow motion across pause: VfxService never sets PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS (unlike AudioDirector/RunFlow/InventoryUI which do), so when the pause menu opens while a hitstop request is active, VfxService._process stops ticking, _update_time_scale never expires the request, and Engine.time_scale stays at ~0.05. Every PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS node (the entire pause menu, audio fades) runs with delta scaled by 0.05 — the pause UI animates in extreme slow motion until unpause. Separately, request_shake accepts a duration_ms parameter it completely ignores (decay is purely the lerp in _process), a dead contract callers are tuning against.
action: Make VfxService process during pause and either honor or remove the shake duration parameter.
location: apps/game/client/scripts/art/vfx/vfx_service.gd (Lines 55-79 / _ready and _process lifecycle, missing process_mode; Lines 736-743 / request_shake ignoring duration_ms)
implementation: 1) In _ready add: process_mode = Node.PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS (the sweep/time-scale bookkeeping already uses wall-clock Time.get_ticks_msec, so it is pause-safe). 2) Belt-and-braces: when MenuStack pauses, refuse new gameplay time-scale pushes (in push_time_scale: if get_tree().paused: return for gameplay ids). 3) request_shake: either implement duration by storing _shake_until_ms and zeroing _shake_amount at expiry in _process, or delete the parameter and update all call sites (grep 'request_shake(') so the API stops lying.

problem: TIER2/PERF (VFX) — get_death_burst_lifetime is a static helper that re-loads and re-parses the effects JSON from disk (ContentLoader.load_json(EFFECTS_PATH)) on every call, while the instance path (_max_burst_lifetime_for_effect) already has the parsed _effects dictionary cached. Death bursts happen once per enemy kill — in wave mode that is a disk read + full JSON parse per kill on the main thread.
action: Cache the computed lifetime in a static var, or route the static callers through the autoload's cached _effects.
implementation: static var _death_burst_lifetime := -1.0; static func get_death_burst_lifetime() -> float: if _death_burst_lifetime >= 0.0: return _death_burst_lifetime; ...existing computation...; _death_burst_lifetime = max_lifetime; return max_lifetime. If ContentLoader gains the memoizing cache proposed in the earlier content-preload entry this becomes cheap automatically, but the one-line static cache is still worth it to skip the per-kill dictionary walk.

problem: TIER2/PERF (UI) — CombatHUD and InventoryUI both run unconditional per-frame _process handlers (combat_hud.gd line 294, inventory_ui.gd line 343) with InventoryUI additionally set to PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS, so a full-screen inventory keeps ticking while paused AND the HUD polls every frame even when nothing changed; InventoryUI also rebuilds grids/rows via child.queue_free() loops on refresh (lines 119, 170, 633, 976, 1118) instead of reusing nodes — GC churn on every inventory change and rapid status ticks.
action: Convert per-frame polling into signal-driven updates with dirty flags, and reuse row/cell nodes instead of free-and-rebuild.
location: apps/game/client/scripts/ui/combat_hud.gd (Line 294 / _process) and apps/game/client/scripts/ui/inventory_ui.gd (Lines 71, 343 / process_mode + _process; Lines 119, 170, 633, 976, 1118 / queue_free rebuild loops)

There is no re-entrancy guard in unbind_boss.

location: apps/game/client/scripts/ui/combat_hud.gd (Lines 335-375 / bind_boss connections and unbind_boss disconnections)

problem: TIER3/QUALITY (WEB) — patchNotes ordering relies on localeCompare(..., { numeric: true }) over free-form version strings: suffixed versions ('0.4.0-hotfix1', '0.10.0-beta') sort by locale string rules where the numeric flag only helps digit runs, so non-plain-semver slugs misorder the patch-notes index; getPatchNote also looks up by version while parsePatchNote's slug may differ (data.slug ?? data.version), so a custom slug makes the detail page 404 its own list entry.
action: Sort by parsed semver tuple with a date fallback, and route detail lookups by the same slug the list renders.
location: apps/web/src/content/loader.ts (Lines 52-58 / patchNotes sort; Lines 60-66 / getPatchNote lookup) and apps/web/src/pages/PatchNoteDetail.tsx (consumer)
implementation: function semverKey(v: string): number[] { const m = /^(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)/.exec(v); return m ? [+m[1], +m[2], +m[3]] : [0, 0, 0]; } sort: (a, b) => { const ka = semverKey(a.version), kb = semverKey(b.version); for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) if (ka[i] !== kb[i]) return kb[i] - ka[i]; return b.date.localeCompare(a.date); }. Change getPatchNote(slugOrVersion) to match entry.slug first, falling back to entry.version, and make PatchNotes.tsx link with entry.slug so list and detail always agree.
